C08-M01-L02-F1.title: Roles inside a SOC
C08-M01-L02-F1.caption: The SOC manager is accountable for six role groups: the shift team, responders, specialists and three engineering roles.
C08-M01-L02-F1.alt: Tree diagram. Root: SOC manager, accountable for the service. Six children: Shift lead + SOC analysts (triage, cases, first response); Incident responders (scope, coordinate, recommend); Hunters, forensics, malware (specialist depth, Tier 3); Detection engineers (rules, tests, tuning, ATT&CK); Threat intelligence (relevant threats into detections); Platform + SOAR engineers (ingestion, retention, automation).
C08-M01-L02-F1.note: A responsibility map, not a headcount chart: one person may hold several boxes, but every box needs an owner.

C08-M01-L02-F2.title: Example SOC RACI (fictional Banyan Microfinance)
C08-M01-L02-F2.caption: Who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for six common activities, with exactly one Accountable per row.
C08-M01-L02-F2.alt: Table with columns Activity, SOC analyst, Incident responder, IT ops / identity, Legal / compliance. Triage and disposition: A/R, I, -, -. Declare an incident: C, A/R, -, I. Isolate endpoint (EDR, pre-agreed): R, A, I, -. Reset account / revoke sessions: I, C, A/R, -. Rebuild or restore a server: I, C, A/R, -. CERT-In report decision (6 h): C, C, -, A/R.
C08-M01-L02-F2.note: R = Responsible, A = Accountable (one per row), C = Consulted, I = Informed. Each organisation agrees its own matrix.
